title: Compatibility comparator, artifact list and intentional-break drill (I18, D26)
summary: Builds the I18 comparison: root `compatibility.json` (artifact list and a provisional candidate pointer), `bin/api-compat.php` with the rule set of p4-execution#compatibility, composer script `api:compat`, the unit catalogue of intentional breaks with allowed-addition controls in `tests/Arch/CompatibilityTest.php`, and `bin/compat-drill.sh`, which proves on real code patches in a throwaway clone that the stable-tag comparison rejects the five required breaks.
why: D26 and phase V1 (every intentional break is rejected); a regenerated manifest proves only freshness (phase pitfall). Hard risks: a missing rule lets a break through silently after 1.0; an over-strict rule teaches people to replace the baseline; internal check FQCNs used as JSON keys in doctor-checks.json mistaken for identities; implementer vs consumer rules (renames allowed only for spi-implement interface methods, I20) inverted; the drill creating tags in the real repository.

include: `compatibility.json` exactly as p4-execution#compatibility (all 22 artifacts incl. 8 DDL rows); `candidate` = the sha HEAD has before this item's first commit (provisional; P4.8 replaces it)

`bin/api-compat.php`: CLI `--against=<ref>|auto`, `--json`; baseline resolution; JSON-only reading through `git show`; every PHP and format rule id of p4-execution#compatibility; exit codes 0/1/2; functions loadable by a test without running the CLI (same pattern as `bin/api-manifest.php` in `ApiManifestTest`)
Root `composer.json` script `api:compat`; add it to `composer check` after `api:check`
`tests/Arch/CompatibilityTest.php`: the unit catalogue of p4-execution#breaks (one case per rule id, controls, tag-selection cases)
`bin/compat-drill.sh` per p4-execution#breaks (D1–D5 rejected, D6 accepted, main repository tags unchanged); evidence `plans/2026.10.10-№1-AZGUARD-CORE-STABILIZATION/artifacts/evidence/P4/drill.md`
`tests/Arch/invariants.json`: I18 `status: exists`, `checks: [tests/Arch/CompatibilityTest.php, bin/api-compat.php, bin/compat-drill.sh]`, blocking stays `after P4` (P4.8 sets `now`)

If the manifest lacks a fact a rule needs (e.g. the literal default value of a parameter), extend `bin/api-manifest.php` minimally, regenerate both manifests with `composer api:manifest` and note it in the result
exclude: CI workflows and the PR guard (P4.5)
A major-version escape hatch (future release decision)

Exact commands, PHP 8.4 shim, driver ports, composer update rule, CI evidence procedure
Normative comparator design: inputs, CLI, baseline resolution, every rule id, format semantics, pointer
What is stable: consumer vs implementer, named arguments, additions, enums, formats, generator and comparison
Conventions: attributes, positional Implement calls, generics are part of the contract
Frozen event payload state keys (a format break example)
Every identity is frozen at the candidate

Manifest fields the comparator reads; test-loading pattern

task_files.note: only if an in-memory mutation is not enough
only if a rule needs a missing fact

rules: Do not stage, revert or overwrite the owner's uncommitted files (p4-execution#conventions item 6); commit only the item's paths.
The comparator never executes or autoloads baseline code; it compares JSON only.
Every rule id has a unit case that fails when the rule is removed (negative control), and every allowed addition has a control that stays green.
The drill never creates, moves or deletes a tag in the main repository; it asserts this at the end.
guidance: Structure the comparator as pure functions: `compatBaseline(string $against): array{ref, sha}`, `compatLoad(string $ref, string $path): array`, `compatApi(array $base, array $current): array{breaks, additions}`, `compatFormat(string $id, array $base, array $current, array $context): array{…}`. Key manifest classes by `name`, members by name, parameters by position (rename = same position, different name). A method is 'overridable' when its type is not final and the method is not final (protected included) or the type is `spi-implement`. For the commands synopsis write a small parser for Symfony synopsis strings (`<arg>`, `[<arg>]`, `<arg>...`, `[--opt]`, `[--opt [OPT]]`, `[--opt OPT]`, `-s|--opt`). Keep output stable and sorted so CI logs diff well. The manifests are large (core ~900 KB): never read them whole; query entries with python3/jq (e.g. publication, enum and namedArguments of one class) to pick the catalogue targets.

validation.expect: exit 0 (HEAD compatible with the provisional candidate)
exit 0: D1–D5 rejected with their rule ids, D6 accepted, main repository tags unchanged

validation.cmd: composer analyse && composer lint:check && composer refactor:check && composer api:check
